expect.text: Expect it in a data engineer interview, next to sequel that goes a level deeper than an analyst screen.

probe.text: Interviewers probe four things, from the query down to the files.

probe-sql.text: Advanced sequel: window functions, qualify, deduplication, gaps and islands, and incremental logic.

probe-model.text: Data modeling: star or snowflake schemas, facts and dimensions, normalization trade-offs, and slowly changing dimensions.

probe-pipe.text: Pipelines and orchestration: batch or streaming, idempotency, backfills, and scheduling in Airflow or Dagster.

probe-store.text: And systems and formats: columnar files like Parquet, partitioning and file sizes, warehouse or lakehouse, and cost.

ai.text: AI has changed this interview in four ways.

ai-rag.text: Ingestion for retrieval-augmented generation, or RAG, is now a system design prompt: parse, chunk, embed, index, and keep it fresh incrementally, like any other pipeline.

ai-vector.text: Vector search trade-offs: exact or approximate, Postgres or a dedicated store, metadata filters, and hybrid keyword search.

ai-gov.text: Governance for AI data: permissions checked at query time, deletions that reach the vectors, and personal data kept from outside embedding APIs.

ai-code.text: And AI-written pipeline code needs review for idempotency, time zones and schema drift. Some coding rounds now allow an assistant, so ask the recruiter about each one.

series.text: This series follows the track: eleven videos and a hundred and fifty-seven questions, each answered once. Sequel and data modeling take two videos each.

series-how.text: Each video works through the questions worth a figure, and most end on a quick round of one-line answers.

practice.text: Every topic page has concept checks, three add challenges that run in the browser, and a bank of a hundred and ten multiple-choice questions covers the whole track.

next.text: Nearly every loop has hard sequel, so the series starts there. Next: sequel, window functions and query patterns.
